researcher_notes: Woodside took the Final Investment Decision on the foundational phase of Louisiana LNG (Calcasieu Parish, LA; 3-train, 16.5 Mtpa) on 29 April 2025. Project formerly known as Driftwood LNG, acquired by Woodside via its 2024 Tellurian acquisition. FID year confirmed by Woodside's own media release (sponsor/primary) and independent trade press (LNG Prime); NS Energy project page (Wayback) corroborates. Two+ independent sources, year explicit.

Magnolia LNG (Lake Charles, LA; subsidiary of Australia's Liquefied Natural Gas Ltd / LNGL) was publicly proposed in 2013, announced by Gov. Bobby Jindal and Magnolia LNG as a $2.2bn export facility at the Port of Lake Charles. The Lake Charles site was leased in Dec 2012, with the public project announcement in 2013. Year confirmed by Louisiana Economic Development (state/primary announcement) and independent maritime press (gCaptain).

Enterprise Products Partners' Morgan's Point ethane export terminal (Houston Ship Channel / La Porte, TX) began service in 2016 — commissioning/startup July 2016, first export cargo (M/V JS INEOS Intrepid, ~265,000 bbl to INEOS Rafnes, Norway) loaded September 2016. Commercial-operations year = 2016, confirmed by three independent publishers (Argus, Tanks & Terminals, Construction Boxscore).

This is the Mt. Airy, LA marine terminal (St. John the Baptist Parish), which physically began operating when Pin Oak Terminals opened it on 16-17 August 2017 (Phase 1; construction from late 2015). MPLX acquired the asset from Pin Oak Holdings in September 2018 — so the terminal's operating-start = 2017, while MPLX ownership dates from 2018. GEM appears to track the same physical asset under both 'MPLX Mount Airy Terminal' and 'Pin Oak Terminal'. If GEM intends operating-under-MPLX, that would be 2018; commissioning of the terminal itself = 2017. Year 2017 confirmed by Mercuria (lead investor/primary) and Louisiana Economic Development (state).

LPG export from Sunoco Logistics' (now Energy Transfer) Nederland, TX terminal began via the Mariner South project; the first propane export cargo loaded out of Nederland in February 2015 (S&P Global Platts, 17 Feb 2015 — bot-blocked, no Wayback snapshot available, so not stagable). Only one independently accessible source verified (Butane-Propane News / bpnews, non-primary trade), hence tier low. The Nederland marine terminal itself is decades older (Sun Oil era); 2015 reflects the LPG-export operating start, which is the gas-relevant milestone.

Could not verify a defensible single operating-start year. The NuStar North Beach Terminal (Port of Corpus Christi) predates all documented dated milestones: NuStar absorbed Kaneb's terminal assets in 2005; a marine loading dock was completed Feb 2014 (capacity tripled to 400,000 bpd); the first post-export-ban US crude export cargo loaded there in Dec 2015 (NuStar/ConocoPhillips); and NuStar bought additional North Beach assets in a $93M deal in Dec 2016. Each is an expansion/export milestone, not the terminal's original commissioning, and no original operating-start year is publicly documented. Marking UNRESOLVED rather than asserting an expansion year as the operating start.

NuStar's St. James (LA) crude/products storage terminal became operational in 2006 per Offshore-technology market data (sole verifiable source, an aggregator, fetched via Wayback because the live page is bot-blocked). NuStar is a 2007 spin-off of Valero's midstream assets; St. James was built out in phases (the cited 'St. James IV' implies later phase expansions) from ~2006. Single non-primary source, so tier low; could not independently corroborate the 2006 date.

The Phillips 66 Beaumont Terminal (Gulf Coast crude/products terminal in the Beaumont/Nederland, TX area) was originally established by Smith Bluff Pure Oil Co. on 5 April 1923; Phillips 66 held a centennial celebration on 5 April 2023 ('100 years to the day'). The terminal passed Pure Oil -> Unocal (1960s) -> Chevron (1990s) -> Phillips 66 (acquired June 2014). 'Began operating'/commissioning = 1923; if GEM intends the current-owner start, that would be 2014. One verified non-primary source (Port Arthur News) for the 1923 founding (the trerc.tamu.edu corroborating article is bot-blocked with no Wayback snapshot), hence tier low.

Pin Oak Terminals' multi-product liquid marine terminal at Mt. Airy, LA (St. John the Baptist Parish, Mississippi River) opened 16-17 August 2017 (Phase 1; construction began late 2015 after Mercuria's Dec 2016 investment). Operating-start = 2017, confirmed by Mercuria (key investor/primary) and Louisiana Economic Development (state). NB: this is the same physical asset later sold to MPLX in Sept 2018 (see GEM 'MPLX Mount Airy Terminal' record) — GEM appears to carry it twice.

Plains All American began building its St. James (LA) crude terminal in 2004; the initial ~3.5 MMbbl storage phase became operational in Q1 2007 (RBN Energy, fetched via Wayback because the live page is bot-blocked). Subsequent expansions followed (Mississippi River dock 2009, rail receipt 2010, +1.2 MMbbl 2012). Operating-start = 2007. Single non-primary analyst source verified (OGJ's 2004 planning article and the Plains/BusinessWire releases are bot-blocked with no Wayback snapshots), hence tier low.
